summary: Each member mirrors the stream items its messages shard holds, and its own lifecycle steps for them, into the graph's file, so the graph's idle-mail, unread-mail, held-mail and usage indexes count stream mail as they count graph mail; a stream send with an idempotency key replays instead of writing a second item; members advertise messages_stream_mirror=1 (db break-up step 4c-2a-1). Nothing in the product writes stream mail yet, so this changes nothing a user sees until a later release routes mail to the stream.

replay.detail: No claim is written or projected differently. The mirror is local and rebuilt from the shard; graph claims fold as before, and a subject the graph also holds is counted from the graph.

schema.detail: New member-local tables in the graph's file: local_stream_sent and local_stream_lifecycle, with triggers that fold into local_idle_messages and unread_mail and queue held-mail and usage work, and two cursors in meta (stream_mirror_sent_through, stream_mirror_lifecycle_through). New member-local table stream_operations in the messages shard's file. No user_version change, no change to any replicated table; none of them replicates or is in a digest. The unread, held-mail, relayed backlog and usage reads also read local_stream_sent and local_stream_lifecycle.

rules.detail: No admission rule changes. A stream append under an idempotency key now returns the item the key already wrote (appended=false) for the same request and refuses another request with idempotency-mismatch, as a graph append does. The key is kept in the shard's local stream_operations table, not in the item, so the item a keyed send writes is byte for byte what an unkeyed one writes and a release that holds the shard admits and digests it alike.

compatibility.detail: Additive. The daemon.started feature messages_stream_mirror=1 is informational: no member routes on it, and messages_stream_inbox (4c-2a-3) will name a complete inbox. Every member mirrors every item its shard holds, whoever the recipient, so members that hold the same mail count it alike; a member of a release without the mirror (v0.3.28 and earlier) counts only graph mail, as before, and admits keyed items with no invalid record. Upgraded in place, a member mirrors what its shard already held at its first start.

downtime.detail: No migration: the tables are created empty and the daemon mirrors the shard in pages of 500 after it starts, off the startup path.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to a release without the mirror leaves the mirror's tables unread: the release keeps counting what the mirror already put in its indexes, and its reads count no stream mail that arrives or is read meanwhile, so during the rollback its unread and held counts can include stream mail read since. Upgraded again, the mirror resumes from its cursors and catches up. A backup carries neither the mirror nor stream_operations: the restored member rebuilds the mirror from the restored shard when its daemon starts, and a stream send retried after a restore writes its item again.
